title: Redesign the Operator's Board — re-roll 2 (sidebar)
question: Every hand now carries your pinned sidebar. Lock the one that organizes it right — or steer and re-roll again.

options.label: The Index Rail
options.lineage: library card index / patch-cord cross-reference frame
options.thesis: The sidebar is the index of lines — name plus state lamp, selectable — and the selected line's full detail is always open beside it: status, usage, embed, actions. Zero navigation.
options.viewport: Header, then the rail with every line as an index card and the main pane holding the selected line's detail at full width — board, meter, and embed in one unbroken view.
options.risk: With many lines the rail scrolls and the 'everything at once' feel thins out.

regions.label: index rail · every line, lamp + name
selected line detail · status, meter, embed, actions

options.label: The Fleet Board
options.lineage: machine-room meter panel mounted beside the board
options.thesis: The sidebar is the meter panel — plan gauge, credits, limits, and alerts permanently on — and the main area stays pure board: every line, nothing else.
options.viewport: Header, then the meter sidebar with the usage position always visible, and the jack rows filling the main pane edge to edge.
options.risk: The sidebar answers 'how am I doing' but not 'what happened recently'.

options.label: The Wizard Rail
options.lineage: job ticket rail on a workshop wall
options.thesis: Creation becomes a permanent instrument: the sidebar carries the create-a-line flow step by step, always one click from the board it feeds.
options.viewport: Header, then the create rail with the four steps stacked and the board beside it — starting a new line never leaves the view.
options.risk: It rebuilds the creation flow you said you already like — locking it changes the wizard.
